extracted.intended_audience: general educated readers interested in satire, religion, and criticism of Mary Baker G. Eddy/Christian Science
extracted.subtask_description: A satirical essay/chapter that analyzes and lampoons the by-laws, governance, and doctrinal rules of Mary Baker G. Eddy's Christian Science organization, highlighting formal requirements, penalties, and the concentration of authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clerk understanding requirement / resignation penalty
rubrics_metrics.description: Clerk must obtain a clear understanding of a communication before presenting it to the Church; 'Failing to adhere to this By-law, the Clerk must resign.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Twain comments that this By-law grew out of an upsetting incident and implies it is onerous and comically phrased; he imagines a clerk misunderstanding Mrs. Eddy's language and being driven mad. The passage functions as an operational rule (understand then present) with an automatic resignation penalty for noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readers' qualifications and duties (discontiguous treatment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles III and IV set forth in much detail the qualifications and duties of Readers, but the subject is revisited later in the By-laws, suggesting disorder or artifice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Twain notes the By-laws' apparent pretence of order but actual clumsiness ('jumbulacious') and implies the detailed rules concentrate power in Mrs. Eddy. This signals that Readers are tightly governed and that procedural presentation is inconsistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pastor Emeritus power to remove or appoint Readers globally
rubrics_metrics.description: In any Church. Sec. 2. The Pastor Emeritus of the Mother-Church shall have the right (through a letter addressed to the individual and Church of which he is the Reader) to remove a Reader from this office in any Church of Christ, Scientist, both in America and in foreign nations; or to appoint the Reader to fill any office belonging to the Christian Science denomination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Twain emphasizes that removal or appointment requires no charges, no explanation, and no recourse; a single letter effects dismissal. He contrasts this absolute authority with even the Pope's powers and highlights its arbitrary, worldwide reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: By-law unamendability except by Pastor Emeritus consent
rubrics_metrics.description: This By-law can neither be amended nor annulled, except by consent of the Pastor Emeritus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Twain satirically remarks on the improbability of Mrs. Eddy ever giving such consent, underscoring the permanence and iron control the clause creates over church governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership doctrine source restriction (monopoly of texts)
rubrics_metrics.description: First qualification for membership: belief in the doctrines of Christian Science 'according to the platform and teaching contained in the Christian Science text-book, "Science and Health, with Key to the Scriptures," by Rev. Mary Baker G. Eddy.' 'The Bible and the above--named book [Science and Health], with other works by the same author,' must be his only text-books for the commerce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Twain explains this as an enforced doctrinal monopoly: no commentaries or alternative exegeses are permitted; Mrs. Eddy's works alone are the authorized sources, preventing independent interpretation and consolidating doctrinal authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on independent explanations/commentaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Mrs. Eddy's words are to be the sole elucidators of the Bible and Science and Health--no other persons' explanations are permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Twain points out the practical effect: it 'squelches independent inquiry' and prevents competing opinions; any explanations by others would need Mrs. Eddy's approval and copyrighting before publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to declare authorship when quoting sacred revelations or poems
rubrics_metrics.description: When Mrs. Eddy's 'sacred revelations' or 'poems of our Pastor Emeritus' are read in public, their authorship must be named; members shall also instruct their students to advertise the authorship when reading those poems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Twain notes this is enforced 'for the good of our Cause' and jokes that it protects Mrs. Eddy's authorship (and the Cause) rather than the reader; he implies the rule is part of constant self-promotion and control of credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Property reconveyance clause (Church edifice deed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sec. 10 (of the deed): 'Whenever said Directors shall determine that it is inexpedient to maintain preaching, reading, or speaking in said church in accordance with the terms of this deed, they are authorized and required to reconvey forthwith said lot of land with the building thereon to Mary Baker G. Eddy, her heirs and assigns forever, by a proper deed of conveyance.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Twain explains this as a safeguard that lets Mrs. Eddy reclaim property at will; he stresses that boards and directors are effectively her instruments, so the clause secures her control of valuable property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required daily prayer from By-laws
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief and good prayer is furnished in the book of By-laws; 'The Scientist is required to pray it every day.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Twain presents this as another prescriptive ritual: the organization mandates daily recitation, which he frames as part of the formal controls imposed on members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopted (amended) Lord's Prayer wording in Science and Health
rubrics_metrics.description: Science and Health's rendering of the Lord's Prayer (1902 edition) rewrites phrases (e.g., 'Our Father-Mother God'..., 'Give us grace for to-day; feed the famished affections'..., 'Love leadeth us not into temptation, but delivereth from sin, disease, and death.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Twain critiques the textual changes, noting doctrinal shifts (e.g., turning 'lead us not into temptation' into an assertion) and laments 'watering down' traditional forms; he treats this as one more sign of doctrinal revisioning under the movement's authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working Against the Cause (unpardonable sin) and permanent expulsion
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Working Against the Cause. Sec. 2. If a member of this Church shall work against the accomplishment of what the Discoverer and Founder of Christian Science understands is advantageous to the individual, to this Church, and to the Cause of Christian Science'--the member is expelled ('drop forever the name of this member from its records').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Twain emphasizes that independent thought or action contrary to what the Founder 'understands' is grounds for immediate and permanent exclusion; he lampoons the prohibition of thinking and the exclusion's irrevocability except by unanimous vote of all the First Members (i.e., effectively Mrs. Eddy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule change limitation for unpardonable sin (requires unanimous First Members)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'This rule cannot be changed, amended, or annulled, except by unanimous vote of all the First Members.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Twain points out the irony: the single person who in practice is the First Member (Mrs. Eddy) renders the rule effectively permanent and self-protecting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ban on practice of hypnotism and sole-complaint procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: By-law forbids Members to practice hypnotism; procedure: (1) If a member is found to be a mental practitioner, (2) Complaint is to be entered against him, (3) By the Pastor Emeritus, and by none else; (4) No member is allowed to make complaint to her in the matter; (5) Upon Mrs. Eddy's mere 'complaint'--unbacked by evidence or proof, and without giving the accused a chance to be heard--his name shall be dropped from this Church.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Twain condemns this as the 'Sole-Witness Court'—Mrs. Eddy as sole accuser, witness, judge, and executioner—and ridicules the lack of due process. He quotes Mrs. Eddy's claim of a spiritual sense enabling her to discern malice, presenting it as justification for unilateral expulsions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic excommunication for failing to read Mrs. Eddy's letter in full
rubrics_metrics.description: If a member carries a letter from Mrs. Eddy to the congregation and forgets to read it or fails to read the whole of it, the By-law reads its transgressor out of the Church.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Twain uses this to illustrate petty, jealousy-driven penalties: a trivial oversight becomes grounds for expulsion, showing the By-laws' pettiness and severity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dishonesty admonition and excommunication
rubrics_metrics.description: Dishonest members are to be admonished; if they continue in dishonest practices, excommunication follows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Twain notes the ironic humor that this By-law on honesty exists given the drafter, and treats it as a conventional moral rule within an otherwise arbitrary code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enumerated offences punishable by excommunication
rubrics_metrics.description: Listed offences whose infringement is punishable by excommunication include: Silence Enjoined; Misteaching; Departure from Tenets; Violation of Christian Fellowship; Moral Offences; Illegal Adoption; Broken By-laws; Violation of By-laws; Formulas Forbidden; Official Advice; Unworthy of Membership; Final Excommunication; Organizing Churches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Twain presents this catalogue to show the breadth of behaviors that can trigger expulsion—ranging from doctrinal deviations to administrative infractions—and comments on the apparent inventiveness devoted to devising ways to 'get rid of her Church members.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Hymnal inclusion and compulsory singing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Christian Science Hymnal entrance closed in 1898; hymns must be approved by the Pastor Emeritus. Mrs. Eddy contributed three hymns; By-law requires singing one of her three hymns in the Mother Church 'as often as once each month.' If a solo singer neglects or refuses to sing one of those three hymns as often as once a month (or more if directed), the singer's salary shall be stopped.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Twain comments this is a measure born of experience to prevent singers from avoiding Mrs. Eddy's hymns; he satirizes forced repetition and the penalty (salary stoppage) as evidence of coercive control and self-promotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board of Education composition and Mrs. Eddy's control
rubrics_metrics.description: Board of Education consists of four members, one of whom is President; its members are elected annually—'Subject to Mrs. Eddy's approval.' Mrs. Eddy is President of the Metaphysical College; if she vacates, the Directors (i.e., Mrs. Eddy) 'shall' elect to the vacancy the President of the Board of Education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Twain points out the circularity: she gives up ‘shadow’ authority but retains substantive control; boards exist but are effectively owned and controlled by Mrs. Eddy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Teachers admission examination requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must pass a thorough three days' examination before the Board of Education 'in Science and Health, chapter on "Recapitulation"; the Platform of Christian Science; page 403 of Christian Science Practice, from line second to the second paragraph of page 405; and page 488, second and third paragraphs.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Twain reports the precise, text-focused exam syllabus, showing reliance on fixed scriptural/textual mastery as the basis for credentialing teachers; he implies the process is tightly controlled by specified passages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board of Lectureship territorial assignment and approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Lecturers are assigned an appointed territory (North, South, East, West, Canada, Great Britain, etc.) and 'must stick to his own territory and not forage beyond its boundaries.' Members of the Board of Lectureship are elected annually 'Subject to the approval of Rev. Mary Baker G. Eddy.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Twain infers that lectures and lecturers are vetted and controlled by Mrs. Eddy and that content and movement are restricted; he suggests no lecture is delivered without her examination and approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Missionaries: limited number and annual election
rubrics_metrics.description: There are but four missionaries; they are elected annually and, like other officers, are subject to Mrs. Eddy's control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Twain observes the scarcity of stable positions and frames missionaries and other officials as temporary servants under Mrs. Eddy's supervision, underlining centralization of authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Branch Churches forbidden to use the By-laws
rubrics_metrics.description: The By-laws state that the branch Churches are strictly forbidden to use them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Twain argues this is practical nonsense—the By-laws are the master's commands to servants and not intended for branch usage; he presents the forbidding as redundant and symptomatic of top-down control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creed copyrighted and immutable
rubrics_metrics.description: The Creed is copyrighted and 'No Change. It is forbidden to change the Creed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Twain notes the copyrighting and prohibition on change as a method of control over doctrine and authorship; he treats the copyright as another device to prevent any challenge or alteration.
